threads.thread_goal: Align on current cleaning and changeover practices and main issues.

messages.text: Team, let's kick off the Cross-Line Hygiene project. To start, can everyone share how they currently handle cleaning and changeovers? We need to map out the existing steps for both the food and metal lines as per T1 and T2. Let's also note down any pain points.
On my line, we usually just hose everything down, then use the standard sanitizer. The changeover from savory to sweet snacks takes the longest because of the seasoning dust.
Same for me. We follow the chart on the wall. Pre-rinse, foam, scrub, final rinse. The main issue is the floor drains backing up sometimes during the final rinse, which slows us down.
Yeah the seasoning is a pain. Sometimes I'm not sure if I got it all from under the conveyor belt.

For the metal saws, it's a different process. We don't use water. It's a dry cleanup. First, we power down and lock out the machine. Then, we use brushes and an industrial vacuum to get the bulk of the metal chips. The critical part is using compressed air to clear the fine dust from the blade housing and the sensor paths. Any residue there can cause alignment issues. The main problem is that fine aluminum dust gets everywhere, and it's hard to contain it just to our area.

Thanks for that detail, @310108. That's exactly the kind of info we need for T1 and T2. The dust containment is a key risk we need to address.

To test new procedures, we need to pick one food line and one metal saw for a pilot. Any suggestions?
Maybe Line 3 for food? It runs both types of snacks, so it's a good test for changeovers.
For the metal side, I'd suggest Saw #2. It's the one closest to the main walkway between our areas, so it's the highest risk for cross-contamination from foot traffic and forklifts.
Good thinking on Saw #2. That makes sense. So, we're agreed on Food Line 3 and Metal Saw #2 for the pilots.
Excellent. Decision is locked in. Now, for the pilot, we'll use the Time Tracking Sheet A4. What data points should we capture besides just the total time?
Just the time for each step? Like 'rinse time', 'scrub time'?

We should also log any issues or delays encountered during a step. For my area, noting the 'type of metal' being cleaned up would be useful, since steel chips are heavier than aluminum dust and require different handling.
Good point. How about this for A4: 'Step Name', 'Start Time', 'End Time', 'Duration', and a 'Notes/Issues' column. For the metal saw, we can add a 'Material Type' field.
For the food line, maybe a 'Product Type' field for before and after the changeover? Like 'savory to sweet'.

That's a good addition. So to confirm, the time tracking sheet A4 will capture: Step Name, Start/End Time, Duration, Notes/Issues, and a context field (Product Type for food, Material Type for metal). That seems complete.
Perfect. I'll set up the sheet A4 with those columns. I will start drafting the new checklists based on this discussion. Thanks everyone.
ok sounds good
When do we need to start mapping our current steps for T1?
I've already started a draft based on what was said here. I'll share it in a new thread for feedback tomorrow morning. That will cover T1 and T2.

threads.thread_goal: Draft and refine the new cleaning and changeover checklists.

messages.text:
Morning all. As promised, here are the first drafts for the new checklists based on our discussion. Please review and provide feedback.
- Food Line Checklist (draft of A1)
- Metal Saw Checklist (draft of A2)

This is our first step on T3. Let me know if anything is unclear or missing.
Looking at A1, what does 'verify lockout/tagout' mean exactly? Do we need to check something specific?

Good question. It means confirming the machine is fully powered off at the main breaker and has your personal lock on it before you start cleaning. It's a critical safety step. I'll add a note to clarify that in the checklist.

In A1, the 'final rinse' step is before 'inspect for residue'. Shouldn't we inspect before the final rinse? Sometimes if you miss a spot, you have to re-apply the foam, and doing that after the final rinse wastes water.

That's a good point. A better flow would be: 1. Pre-rinse 2. Foam/Scrub 3. Intermediate Rinse 4. Inspect 5. Re-clean if needed 6. Final Sanitizing Rinse. That prevents having to redo the last step. Let's structure A1 that way.
I agree, that's a much more efficient sequence. I'll update A1. With that change, are we happy with the structure for the food line checklist?

Reviewing A2 for the metal saw. The steps are correct, but we should add two points for T6. First, a check for hydraulic fluid leaks around the base of the machine. A small leak can make dust stick and become a bigger problem. Second, we need to specify that the compressed air nozzle must have a pressure regulator set below 30 PSI for safety when cleaning near the blade assembly.
Excellent, @310108. Those are critical safety and maintenance details. I've added them to A2. Anything else for the metal saw checklist?
No, with those additions, the sequence and details in A2 look solid. It covers all the key areas for a proper clean-down.
Great. So we have approval on the structure and sequence for both the food line CIP checklist (A1) and the metal sawing cleaning checklist (A2).
Looks good to me.
Perfect, decisions D3 and D4 are confirmed. I'll finalize these checklists and get them ready for the pilot phase.

threads.thread_goal: Define rules for shared equipment and forklift hygiene between areas.

messages.text: Quick observation from the floor: I just saw one of the shared forklifts come directly from my area, where we've been cutting steel, and head straight into the food packaging zone. Its wheels were covered in metal dust. We need to talk about this.
Wow, that's not good.

Thanks for flagging that immediately, @310108. This is a major contamination risk. This is exactly why we have task T4, to create a unified hygiene checklist for shared equipment. Let's define that now. What are the absolute minimum cleaning steps before a forklift can enter the food area?
The driver should wipe down the forks and maybe the steering wheel?
The wheels are the biggest problem. We should have a station with a brush and maybe a wet mat they have to drive over.

A wet mat will just turn the metal dust into a rusty sludge. A better solution would be a designated blow-down area with compressed air near the metal zone exit. The driver must blow down the wheels, forks, and undercarriage *before* proceeding to the food zone entrance for a final wipe-down. It's a two-stage process.

The two-stage approach is smart. It contains the primary contaminant in the right area. So, let's define the minimum steps as: 1. In the designated zone, use compressed air on wheels/forks. 2. At the food area entrance, wipe down forks and operator controls with a sanitizer wipe. This seems robust but still quick.
Agreed. That's our decision for D5. I'll draft this into the Shared Equipment Checklist A3. Now, how often should we log that this check was done? Every single time feels like a lot of paperwork.
Maybe just once per shift? The first time a driver takes the forklift.
What if different people drive it?

The responsibility should be tied to the equipment, not the person. A simple log on the forklift itself makes sense. The rule is: 'Before entering the food zone, perform the two-step clean and initial the log'. A supervisor can then spot-check the log once per shift to ensure compliance. So the log is continuous, but the formal check is once per shift.

I like that. It's practical and creates accountability. So we're deciding that the log must be initialed before each entry into the food zone, and supervisors will review the logs once per shift. That's our D6.
That works. It puts the responsibility where it should be.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and review pilot runs for new procedures on selected lines.

messages.text: Alright team, the updated checklists are ready. We're set to begin the pilot runs on Food Line 3 and Metal Saw #2, as per T7 and T8. We'll use A4 to track our times. Let's figure out the schedule.
When do we start?
Day shift is usually pretty hectic on Line 3, especially mid-morning. We might not get an accurate time if we're rushed. Maybe the evening or night shift would be better for the first run?
Night shift is quieter, we'd have more time to follow the steps carefully.

For Saw #2, it's best to test after a long run of stainless steel. The chips are stringy and harder to clean than aluminum. That will be the true test of the new procedure. This usually happens on the day shift.

We need data from both busy and quiet times to get a full picture. How about this schedule: Night shift will do the first pilot on Food Line 3 tomorrow. Day shift will do the second pilot on Line 3, and also the first pilot on Metal Saw #2. This gives us varied conditions.

That's a solid plan. It gives us the comparison we need. Let's lock that in. So, to confirm: Pilot starts tomorrow, Night Shift on Line 3 first, then Day Shift on Line 3 and Saw #2. Everyone on those shifts, please be ready to use the new checklist and fill out the time tracking sheet A4.
Got it. I'm on day shift tomorrow, will do it on Line 3.
--- Day passes ---
We did the pilot on night shift. The new checklist was easy to follow. It took about 10 minutes longer than usual though. I put the times in A4.

Just finished the day shift pilot on Line 3. It was a bit rushed. I think I forgot to log the time for the 'intermediate rinse' step separately, I just put it all in with the scrub time. Sorry about that. But overall time was about 15 mins longer.
No problem, @102838, thanks for the update. Just try to capture each step next time. The overall time is the most important metric for now. Thanks @558848 for the feedback too.

Pilot on Saw #2 is done. We did it after the stainless steel run. The new procedure worked well, especially the check for hydraulic leaks - we actually found a small drip that maintenance needs to look at. The whole process took 8 minutes longer, but the machine is definitely cleaner and we caught a maintenance issue. I've logged it all in A4.
Catching a leak proves the value of the new checklist. An extra 8-10 minutes seems like a reasonable trade-off for better quality and preventing future downtime. The data in A4 looks very useful.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize procedures, training briefing, and incident logging routine.

messages.text:
Hi team, I've analyzed the pilot data from A4 and consolidated the feedback. The new procedures add about 10-12 minutes to the changeover/cleaning time, but significantly improve the quality and safety, as @310108's experience showed. I think that's a worthwhile investment.

Attached are the proposed final documents for rollout:
- A7: Final Procedure Summary
- A5: Operator Briefing for toolbox talks (T9)
- A6: Hygiene Incident Log (T10)
- A8: Shift Handover Notes

Please review them. The goal is to approve these and set a go-live date.
Looking at the incident log A6. What kind of things are we supposed to write in there? Is it for big problems only?

Not at all. It's for anything, big or small, that affects hygiene or cleaning. For example: 'Foamer nozzle is clogged', 'Ran out of sanitizer at Station B', 'Drain in Line 2 is slow again'. It helps us spot recurring problems.
So we just write it down when we see it?
Exactly. It should take less than a minute. The shift supervisor will review the log daily.
The final procedure for the metal saw in A7 looks good. It includes the safety details we discussed. The briefing in A5 is also clear and to the point. I'm happy with it.
The shift handover notes A8 are a good idea. It will help us know if the previous shift left any cleaning tasks half-finished.

I've reviewed all the documents (A5, A6, A7, A8). They are consistent, clear, and directly address the problems we identified. The briefing A5 is simple enough for a quick toolbox talk. The whole package looks ready for rollout. I propose we set the official go-live date for all shifts for next Monday. This gives supervisors the rest of this week to brief their teams using A5.

Next Monday sounds perfect. That gives everyone time to get up to speed. So, we have our final decision: we approve the procedure summary A7 and related documents, with a full go-live for all shifts next Monday.
I will take on T12 to get printed copies of the final checklists and procedures posted at the relevant work areas by Friday. Great work everyone, this is a big improvement.
